Inclusion Criteria:
  -  Affected children will be recruited if the treating clinician has made a diagnosis of possible Kawasaki disease (even if they do not fulfil the criteria below for Kawasaki disease)
The current standard diagnostic criteria for KD (Circulation 2001 103 335-336 doi: 10

335) are:
The presence of fever  [AND] for at least five days plus four of the following criteria:
  1

right.raw_text:
Changes in the peripheral extremities Acute: erythema  [OR] and oedema of hands  [OR] and feet Convalescent: membranous desquamation of fingertips
  2

Bilateral painless bulbar conjunctival injection without exudate
  4

left.raw_text:
Changes in lips  [OR] and oral cavity: erythema  [OR] and cracking of lips, [OR]  strawberry tongue, [OR]  diffuse injection of oral  [OR] and pharyngeal mucosae
  5
5cm diameter), usually unilateral Patients meeting not all of these criteria may meet the criteria for atypical Kawasaki disease, ie

right.raw_text: if they have fever  [AND] and two or three of the above criteria and elevation of CRP  [OR] or echocardiographic evidence of coronary artery dilatation

left.raw_text: Parents of affected child must be biological parents

right.raw_text:
Exclusion Criteria:
  -  children who do not have a diagnosis of possible Kawasaki disease
